title: Be with Me, Lord, Where'er I Go
description: Be with Me, Lord, Where'er I Go in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 488 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for Divine Help”, where the book credits them to the Christian Psalmist.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be with me, Lord, wher-e'er I go; Teach me what thou wouldst have me do; Show me my weak-ness, let me see I have my power, my all from thee.

lines: Be with me, Lord, where'er I go;
Teach me what thou wouldst have me do;
Show me my weakness, — let me see
I have my power, my all from thee.
Enrich me always with thy love;
Thy signet put upon my breast,
And let thy spirit on me rest.
Assist and teach me how to pray;
What thou abhorr'st that let me flee,
And only love what pleases thee.
O may I never do my will,
But thine, and only thine, fulfil;
Let all my time and all my ways
Be spent and ended to thy praise.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
